text:
If you’ve got outdoor plans today, this is the day to use them. Sunday starts cool but bright, then turns partly sunny and mild, with a high right around 65 and a south breeze building through the afternoon. The lake will get noticeably rougher too, with south winds reaching 15 to 20 knots and waves building to 1 to 3 feet, so keep smaller boats close to shore and plan to be off the broad water before evening.

Rain showers become possible after 2am, then a cold front crosses Monday with a chance of showers, a high near 56, and a gusty west-to-northwest wind. The models are split on how wet Monday gets, from a few showers to a fairly showery morning, so I’d carry the rain jacket and expect a blustery day even if the rain misses you. Monday’s lake conditions turn rough, with northwest winds up to 25 knots and waves building to 2 to 4 feet. Today is the better bet for a waterfront outing, especially before late afternoon.
